quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Tense Backshift
quests.directSpeech: The economist said, "Inflation has been rising steadily since January."
quests.reportedSpeech: The economist said that inflation had been rising steadily since January.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Has been rising' (present perfect continuous, an ongoing trend) backshifts to 'had been rising', preserving the continuous, ongoing meaning; 'had risen' loses that ongoing sense.
quests.nativeTip: Compare 'had been rising' with 'had risen' carefully — one keeps the ongoing sense of the original, the other doesn't.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The economist said, "Inflation has been rising steadily since January."" ➔ "The economist said that inflation had been rising steadily since January."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Tense Backshift
quests.directSpeech: Hiroshi said, "I was writing the report when the power went out."
quests.reportedSpeech: Hiroshi said that he had been writing the report when the power had gone out.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Was writing' (background action) backshifts to 'had been writing', and 'went out' (the interrupting event) backshifts to 'had gone out'.
quests.nativeTip: Compare all three options carefully — only one keeps both the background action and the interrupting event correctly distinguished.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Hiroshi said, "I was writing the report when the power went out."" ➔ "Hiroshi said that he had been writing the report when the power had gone out."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Tense Backshift
quests.directSpeech: Chidinma said, "I have lived in this city for ten years."
quests.reportedSpeech: Chidinma said that she had lived in that city for ten years.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Have lived' (present perfect, ongoing up to now) backshifts to 'had lived', preserving that same sense one step further back in time.
quests.nativeTip: Compare 'had lived' with the simple past 'lived' — one preserves the sense of an ongoing state up to a point, the other only suggests a finished period.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Chidinma said, "I have lived in this city for ten years."" ➔ "Chidinma said that she had lived in that city for ten years."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Pronoun Reference Shift
quests.directSpeech: Bianca told Farida, "Your idea is better than mine."
quests.reportedSpeech: Bianca told Farida that her idea was better than hers.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Your' (Farida's idea) becomes 'her' referring to Farida, and 'mine' (Bianca's idea) becomes 'hers' referring to Bianca.
quests.nativeTip: The pronoun 'her' appears twice with different meanings here — think about which idea belongs to whom.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Bianca told Farida, "Your idea is better than mine."" ➔ "Bianca told Farida that her idea was better than hers."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Pronoun Reference Shift
quests.directSpeech: Emeka told his father, "You always believed in me, and I'll never forget that."
quests.reportedSpeech: Emeka told his father that he had always believed in him and that he would never forget that.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'You' (the father) becomes 'he', 'me' (Emeka) becomes 'him', and 'I' (Emeka) becomes 'he' again — natural reported speech uses pronouns once the context is clear, not repeated names.
quests.nativeTip: Both 'he' pronouns need care — one refers to the father, the other to Emeka — but the natural way to report this uses pronouns for both, not repeated names.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Emeka told his father, "You always believed in me, and I'll never forget that."" ➔ "Emeka told his father that he had always believed in him and that he would never forget that."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Pronoun Reference Shift
quests.directSpeech: Yuna said to her twin sister, "People always confuse us for each other."
quests.reportedSpeech: Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused them for each other.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Us' becomes 'them', referring to both twins together, and 'confuse' backshifts to 'confused'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Us' refers to both twins together — when reported, it becomes a pronoun for that same pair, not a comparison between two separate people.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Yuna said to her twin sister, "People always confuse us for each other."" ➔ "Yuna told her twin sister that people always confused them for each other."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The trainer said, "You should try doing squats before running."
quests.reportedSpeech: The trainer advised me to try doing squats before running.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Advised' correctly takes 'me to try', while 'suggested me to try' is a common but incorrect pattern, since 'suggested' cannot be followed directly by an object and an infinitive.
quests.nativeTip: 'Advised' takes an infinitive after the object, while 'suggested' never takes an object directly before an infinitive.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The trainer said, "You should try doing squats before running."" ➔ "The trainer advised me to try doing squats before running."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: The coach said, "Why don't you try stretching before the game?"
quests.reportedSpeech: The coach suggested trying stretching before the game.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Suggested' takes a gerund ('trying'), not an infinitive ('to try'), and this phrasing ('why don't you...?') fits 'suggested' rather than 'advised'.
quests.nativeTip: Recall which verb pattern fits 'suggested' — a gerund, not an infinitive.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The coach said, "Why don't you try stretching before the game?"" ➔ "The coach suggested trying stretching before the game."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: The dietitian said, "I recommend eating more vegetables."
quests.reportedSpeech: The dietitian recommended eating more vegetables.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Recommend eating' becomes 'recommended eating', keeping the gerund pattern; 'recommended to eat' is a common incorrect pattern.
quests.nativeTip: 'Recommended', like 'suggested', is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The dietitian said, "I recommend eating more vegetables."" ➔ "The dietitian recommended eating more vegetables."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Place Expression Shift
quests.directSpeech: The tour guide said, "We'll spend the morning here and the afternoon at the museum across town."
quests.reportedSpeech: The tour guide said that they would spend the morning there and the afternoon at the museum across town.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Here' becomes 'there' since it refers to the guide's current location, while 'across town' stays the same because it's already a specific, named place.
quests.nativeTip: Only the first 'here' refers to the current location — the second location ('across town') doesn't need a place-word change since it's already named.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The tour guide said, "We'll spend the morning here and the afternoon at the museum across town."" ➔ "The tour guide said that they would spend the morning there and the afternoon at the museum across town."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Backshift Exception
quests.directSpeech: The email said, "Please arrive at the venue by 9 AM; doors open at 8:30."
quests.reportedSpeech: The email asked attendees to arrive at the venue by 9 AM and said that doors opened at 8:30.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Open' backshifts to 'opened' as a simple fact about the schedule, not 'would open', which would suggest uncertainty about the future.
quests.nativeTip: Compare backshifting 'open' to 'opened' versus using 'would open' — this describes a fixed schedule, not a future intention.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The email said, "Please arrive at the venue by 9 AM; doors open at 8:30."" ➔ "The email asked attendees to arrive at the venue by 9 AM and said that doors opened at 8:30."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Backshift Exception
quests.directSpeech: Noelle said, "I'll be at the office until 6, then home after that."
quests.reportedSpeech: Noelle said that she would be at the office until 6, then home after that.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'After that' stays the same since it's a general sequencing phrase, not a specific time reference that needs shifting.
quests.nativeTip: 'After that' is already a general connector, not a specific time word like 'today' or 'now' — it doesn't need to change.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Noelle said, "I'll be at the office until 6, then home after that."" ➔ "Noelle said that she would be at the office until 6, then home after that."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: The manager said, "Let's avoid making the same mistake again."
quests.reportedSpeech: The manager suggested avoiding making the same mistake again.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Suggested avoiding' is correct because 'suggested' takes a gerund; 'avoid' also always takes a gerund ('avoid making'), never an infinitive.
quests.nativeTip: 'Avoid' itself is always followed by a gerund, and 'suggested' is too — check both verbs.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The manager said, "Let's avoid making the same mistake again."" ➔ "The manager suggested avoiding making the same mistake again."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Infinitive Structure
quests.directSpeech: The teacher said, "I want everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class."
quests.reportedSpeech: The teacher said that she wanted everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Want' correctly takes 'everyone to finish' (object + infinitive); 'suggested everyone to finish' is not a valid pattern for 'suggested'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Want' takes an object plus an infinitive, unlike 'suggested', which never takes an object directly before a verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The teacher said, "I want everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class."" ➔ "The teacher said that she wanted everyone to finish the exercise by the end of class."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: Anton said, "I don't mind waiting a few extra minutes."
quests.reportedSpeech: Anton said that he didn't mind waiting a few extra minutes.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Mind waiting' stays as a gerund structure after backshifting 'don't' to 'didn't'; 'mind to wait' is never correct.
quests.nativeTip: 'Mind' is always followed by a gerund, never an infinitive.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Anton said, "I don't mind waiting a few extra minutes."" ➔ "Anton said that he didn't mind waiting a few extra minutes."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Universal Truth
quests.directSpeech: Yuna said, "Two plus two equals four."
quests.reportedSpeech: Yuna said that two plus two equals four.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since this is a mathematical truth, 'equals' stays in the present tense; it never needs to backshift.
quests.nativeTip: This is a mathematical fact that never changes — compare it with something that actually needs to backshift.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Yuna said, "Two plus two equals four."" ➔ "Yuna said that two plus two equals four."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: Bashir said, "I broke my arm skiing last winter, and it's still a bit stiff."
quests.reportedSpeech: Bashir said that he had broken his arm skiing the previous winter and that it was still a bit stiff.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Broke' (a completed event) becomes 'had broken', but 'is still stiff' (a current state) still backshifts to 'was still stiff' once fully reported, and 'last winter' becomes 'the previous winter'.
quests.nativeTip: Compare the two clauses carefully: one describes a finished past event, and the other describes a present, ongoing condition being reported.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Bashir said, "I broke my arm skiing last winter, and it's still a bit stiff."" ➔ "Bashir said that he had broken his arm skiing the previous winter and that it was still a bit stiff."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Backshift Exception
quests.directSpeech: The travel guide said, "The museum is closed on Mondays."
quests.reportedSpeech: The travel guide said that the museum is closed on Mondays.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since this is a general, ongoing fact about the museum's schedule, 'is closed' does not need to backshift.
quests.nativeTip: This is a standing schedule that is still true — compare it with something that describes a one-time, finished event.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The travel guide said, "The museum is closed on Mondays."" ➔ "The travel guide said that the museum is closed on Mondays."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Tense Backshift
quests.directSpeech: The doctor said, "You don't need surgery."
quests.reportedSpeech: The doctor said that I didn't need surgery.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Don't need' becomes 'didn't need'; dropping 'don't' would completely reverse the doctor's meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Check carefully that the negative meaning of the original sentence is fully preserved.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The doctor said, "You don't need surgery."" ➔ "The doctor said that I didn't need surgery."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Modal Backshift
quests.directSpeech: Yuna said, "I can't guarantee the shipment will arrive by Friday."
quests.reportedSpeech: Yuna said that she couldn't guarantee the shipment would arrive by Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can't guarantee' becomes 'couldn't guarantee'; removing the negative would incorrectly suggest Yuna made a firm promise.
quests.nativeTip: Losing the word 'not' here would completely change what Yuna actually promised.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Yuna said, "I can't guarantee the shipment will arrive by Friday."" ➔ "Yuna said that she couldn't guarantee the shipment would arrive by Friday."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Modal Backshift
quests.directSpeech: The manager said, "I won't approve this budget unless we cut costs elsewhere."
quests.reportedSpeech: The manager said that he wouldn't approve that budget unless they cut costs elsewhere.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Won't approve' becomes 'wouldn't approve'; dropping the negative would reverse the manager's actual position.
quests.nativeTip: Check that the conditional refusal is preserved exactly, not accidentally turned into an agreement.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The manager said, "I won't approve this budget unless we cut costs elsewhere."" ➔ "The manager said that he wouldn't approve that budget unless they cut costs elsewhere."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reported Warning
quests.directSpeech: The supervisor said, "Don't submit the form without a signature."
quests.reportedSpeech: The supervisor warned the staff not to submit the form without a signature.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Don't submit' becomes 'not to submit', keeping 'not' immediately before 'to' and preserving the warning's negative meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Check both the position of 'not' and whether the negative meaning survives the transformation.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The supervisor said, "Don't submit the form without a signature."" ➔ "The supervisor warned the staff not to submit the form without a signature."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: Halima said, "I don't think this plan will work."
quests.reportedSpeech: Halima said that she didn't think that plan would work.
quests.ruleExplanation: The negative attaches to 'think' in the original ('don't think'), so the most accurate transformation keeps 'didn't think' rather than moving the negative to the second clause.
quests.nativeTip: Only one option matches the exact structure of the original sentence, with the negative attached to the same verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Halima said, "I don't think this plan will work."" ➔ "Halima said that she didn't think that plan would work."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Backshift Exception
quests.directSpeech: The landlord said, "Tenants shouldn't leave without giving notice."
quests.reportedSpeech: The landlord said that tenants shouldn't leave without giving notice.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Shouldn't' remains unchanged since it's already a past-compatible negative modal; it doesn't become 'shouldn't have left', which would refer to one specific completed action instead of a general rule.
quests.nativeTip: 'Shouldn't' stays exactly the same here — check that the negative modal isn't accidentally dropped or over-backshifted.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The landlord said, "Tenants shouldn't leave without giving notice."" ➔ "The landlord said that tenants shouldn't leave without giving notice."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Backshift Exception
quests.directSpeech: The mechanic said, "This could be a problem with the battery."
quests.reportedSpeech: The mechanic said that that could be a problem with the battery.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Could' (possibility) stays unchanged since it's already a past-time modal form, and 'this' becomes 'that'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Could' expressing a guess or possibility is already a past-time form and stays the same — don't confuse it with 'had to', which implies certainty or obligation.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The mechanic said, "This could be a problem with the battery."" ➔ "The mechanic said that that could be a problem with the battery."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Modal Backshift
quests.directSpeech: The employee said, "I can finish this task by myself."
quests.reportedSpeech: The employee said that she could finish that task by herself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can' (ability) backshifts to 'could', and 'this' becomes 'that'; 'must' would incorrectly suggest an obligation rather than a capability.
quests.nativeTip: This 'can' expresses ability, not obligation — compare it with a modal that means something completely different.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The employee said, "I can finish this task by myself."" ➔ "The employee said that she could finish that task by herself."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Modal Backshift
quests.directSpeech: The teacher said, "Students must submit their essays by Friday."
quests.reportedSpeech: The teacher said that students had to submit their essays by Friday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Must' (obligation) backshifts to 'had to'; 'could' would incorrectly suggest submitting was optional rather than required.
quests.nativeTip: This 'must' expresses a firm requirement — compare it with a modal that would suggest it's merely optional.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The teacher said, "Students must submit their essays by Friday."" ➔ "The teacher said that students had to submit their essays by Friday."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: The scientist said, "This theory has been tested repeatedly, and it still holds up."
quests.reportedSpeech: The scientist said that that theory had been tested repeatedly and that it still held up.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'This' becomes 'that', 'has been tested' becomes 'had been tested', and 'holds up' backshifts to 'held up' since it's being reported as part of the scientist's overall claim.
quests.nativeTip: Check every element carefully: the demonstrative, the present perfect, and the ongoing present-tense claim.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The scientist said, "This theory has been tested repeatedly, and it still holds up."" ➔ "The scientist said that that theory had been tested repeatedly and that it still held up."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: The landlord said, "You can't paint the walls without asking me first."
quests.reportedSpeech: The landlord said that I couldn't paint the walls without asking him first.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can't' becomes 'couldn't' (keeping the negative permission intact), 'you' becomes 'I', and 'me' becomes 'him'.
quests.nativeTip: Check both the negative meaning and every pronoun carefully in this review question.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The landlord said, "You can't paint the walls without asking me first."" ➔ "The landlord said that I couldn't paint the walls without asking him first."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: The advisor said, "I recommend that you diversify your portfolio, though the final decision is yours."
quests.reportedSpeech: The advisor said that she recommended diversifying my portfolio, though the final decision was mine.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Recommend that you diversify' becomes 'recommended diversifying' (gerund, not infinitive), 'your' becomes 'my', 'yours' becomes 'mine', and 'is' becomes 'was'.
quests.nativeTip: This final review question checks the gerund pattern after 'recommended', the possessive changes, and the tense in the final clause.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The advisor said, "I recommend that you diversify your portfolio, though the final decision is yours."" ➔ "The advisor said that she recommended diversifying my portfolio, though the final decision was mine."
